(rahugh) 11 a.m. tom and phyllis o’malley marian, eamon and nora gorry adoration of the blessed sacrament - kilbeggan: after mon. morning mass until 11 wednesday 6.30 p.m. until start of mass at 7.30 and rahugh: friday 7 p.m. - 8 p.m. plate collection (17 &18 oct) / mission sunday: €1,640; maintenance: €70; patron offerings: €10. thanks to all who are so generous. catholic newspaper on sale at the entrance for €3.80 per copy . we will have a mass of remembrance for those who have died in the past year on saturday 14th nov. at 7.30pm. there will be candles available at the church entrance for families who were bereaved in the past year, to bring a candle to the table in front of the altar for their deceased loved one as their name is read out during mass. please decide before mass which family member will carry the candle to the table. the death of someone you love is always traumatic. their passing leaves a void in your life and home. we turn to family and friends to console us in our grieving. we also turn to god and his word for consolation. we read in the gospel jesus’ great promise, “trust in god still and trust in me. there are many rooms in my father’s house. ” as a community, we will gather to support each other and turn to god in prayer for our deceased loved ones at our reme mbrance mass. heavenly father, we entrust pope leo to your loving care. grant him strength, comfort, and complete healing as he faces this illness. guide his doctors and bless those caring for him. through the intercession of mary, help of christians, may he recover soon and continue serving your church faithfully. a men. kilbeggan

greater technological advancement than ever before, it is intolerable that bread should be considered a privilege and water a contested commodity. regular access to safe, adequate and sufïcient food, in keeping with the dignity of every person, is a basic human right. guaranteeing this right is an obligation of justice that binds both in dividual states and the internation- al community. and yet, while innovations accelerate production, distribution is being negle cted. grain markets are being optimized on stock exchanges, while the actual seeds that germinate in the soil fall into the hands of monopolies that suffocate small-scale farming. …. the myth that growth can be endless when resources are limited has reached breaking point. today, innovation requires adopting an intergenerational sense of responsibility that looks beyond annual budgets. innovation means re conciling technology with wisdom, including ancestral wisdom, while maintaining a vision for the future. it is not a
